title: Island topography + urbanism
oneLiner: An island's terrain, roads and drainage, rebuilt as native Revit elements.
problem: Planners and architects on a live project needed the island's earthworks and urbanism in Revit, beyond what native terrain tools handle well.
approach: Terrain built in Civil 3D and Rhino, then brought into Revit as native topography, floors, drainage and railings through Rhino.Inside and Grasshopper.
result: One live Revit model with terrain, roads, paving and urban systems, and total earthworks volume calculated in Grasshopper.

title: Stadium façade: BIM to fabrication
oneLiner: One master model that writes every fabrication file.
problem: The client needed a precise Revit model of a stadium's façade structure, and then fabrication models for every piece, normally built in separate software.
approach: I automated both steps with Rhino.Inside Revit and Grasshopper: a full BIM model for clash detection, and scripts that read Revit parameters to export fabrication STP files.
result: When the Revit model changed, the fabrication files updated with it, and no separate fabrication software was needed.

title: Sensi
oneLiner: A copilot that scores how each room will feel, across six senses.
problem: Floor plans get checked for structure, cost and energy, but not for how each room will feel to the person living in it.
approach: It learns a user's sensory profile, scores every room with fixed rules, and lets them edit the plan in plain language. The LLM routes and explains; it never sets the score.
result: Trade-offs like 'bigger window, more noise, colder room' become visible across a whole plan, re-scored live on every edit.
coordination: Led by Emilie El Chidiac. I built the back end and front end and refined the LLM layer.

title: Hyperbuilding + Forma
kind: MaCAD, IAAC, extended with my own APS work
oneLiner: Performance data placed inside the model as geometry, then checked automatically in the cloud.
problem: Three studio teams produced geometry, but no one owned the data, so performance KPIs stayed in spreadsheets.
approach: We set naming and parameter standards, then used Rhino.Inside Revit to place KPI families and fill shared parameters automatically. I'm now checking that standard on the AEC Data Model.
result: Thermal, acoustic and air-quality KPIs readable in the model, with filters, sheets and IFC export.
coordination: I worked at the planning level: the initial standards and the order of work across teams, while my teammates focused on execution and code. The Forma extension is my own work.

title: Computational bucketing
oneLiner: Every element coloured by its value, on every new model version.
problem: Checking how a property spreads across a model meant clicking through elements one by one, and left out anyone without a Speckle account.
approach: A Speckle Automate function groups elements by a chosen property and feeds a web viewer coloured by range.
result: A 25–30 minute model review now takes under three minutes.
